newsitem.title: USA: Lott says pilot Flinn "badly abused" by Air Force.
newsitem.headline: Lott says pilot Flinn "badly abused" by Air Force.

text.p: Senate Republican leader Trent Lott Tuesday said the Pentagon needs to "get in touch with reality" in the case of Air Force First Lt. Kelly Flinn, who faces a court-martial on adultery changes, saying she has been "badly abused" by the Air Force.
"I am concerned about what I have seen happening to Lt. Flinn," Lott told reporters at the White House after a meeting with President Clinton. "I think it's unfair."
"I don't understand why she is being singled out and punished the way she is. I think at a minium she ought to get an honourable discharge," said Lott.
"I tell you, the Pentagon is not in touch with reality on this whole question of fraternisation," Lott told reporters. "I mean, get real. You're still dealing with human beings."

He said he has not raised the issue with Secretary of Defence William Cohen but if the case does not turn out "better than it looks like it's going to be worked out, I am going to take it up with him because I think she has been badly abused."

Flinn, the Air Force's first female B-52 bomber pilot, faces charges including adultery and fraternisation. She admits having an affair with a married civilian and also having sex with a lower-ranking enlisted man, violating the military code of conduct.

Flinn, who is 26 and single, sought to resign from the Air Force with an honourable discharge. The court-martial at Minot Air Force Base in North Dakota was put on hold Tuesday while authorities asked the Pentagon for permission to proceed.
